rationale: The per-site imagery style guide is the platform's brand contract for generated images, and its most identity-bearing field — the palette — is being silently discarded before it reaches the model. composeDirection joins medium -> mood -> palette, so the palette is ALWAYS last, and composeImagePromptWithDirection then truncates the whole composed direction at maxImageryDirectionInPrompt = 200 chars. A verbose medium+mood therefore evicts the colours, and nothing anywhere says so: no warning, no error, and the generated image looks deliberate. Proven live on 2026-07-19: gamesdesign.co.uk's content_hero guide specifies 'cyan #00bcd4 on near-black #121212', and the stored assets.origin_prompt for content_hero_tool_ehp_calculator ends at 'colour palette: near-black ground (#121212).' — the cyan never reached the model. The two generated images came back orange/navy and teal, inconsistent with each other, which is exactly the style-drift failure that failed the D13 owner gate in July. This is not a site-config mistake: robot-hands.com, the testbed whose imagery PASSED that gate, composes to 233 chars and is also truncated — it only looks correct because its cut happens to fall AFTER 'electric blue (#0080FF)'. The difference between the fleet's good site and its bad one is where a character count landed. I mitigated in config (terse medium/mood, accent first, bringing three sites to 139-147 chars) and confirmed the fix end-to-end: the regenerated prompt carries the full palette and the regenerated images are correctly cyan-on-near-black and consistent with each other. But config phrasing discipline is not a fix — the next site with an expressive medium silently loses its colours again. This plan makes the palette structurally survivable. It deliberately does NOT raise the cap; see risks.

plan.summary: The imagery style guide's palette is composed last and then truncated away by a 200-char cap, so brand colours silently never reach the image model; the model then invents an accent. Reorder composeDirection to put the palette FIRST — it is the shortest and most identity-bearing of the three fields, so it is the one that must survive a truncation — and make the truncation observable at the call site instead of silent. Adds unit coverage for the truncation-survival property, which currently has none.

edits.rationale: Palette is the shortest field and the one carrying brand identity; medium and mood are prose and degrade gracefully when clipped. Ordering it first makes the truncation lose the expendable half instead of the load-bearing half. This is a one-line reordering with no behavioural change when the direction fits inside the cap, which is the common case.

The truncation is currently invisible: the existing log prints a 100-char direction_preview, which is SHORTER than the 200-char cap, so it can never show that anything was dropped. That invisibility is why this defect survived a passed owner gate and got written into the runbook as a false lesson about `avoid`. A dropped brand instruction should be greppable after the fact, and the fields make the DB-side evidence (assets.origin_prompt) interpretable.
edits.sketch:
if direction != "" {
	composed := composeImagePromptWithDirection(promptTemplate, direction)
	truncated := len(direction) > maxImageryDirectionInPrompt
	if truncated {
		// bugs_open/027 4b: a silently clipped direction reads as a
		// deliberate style choice in the output. Say so, with what was lost.
		params.Logger.Warn("Imagery direction TRUNCATED before generation",
			zap.String("site_id", siteID),
			zap.String("kind", kind),
			zap.Int("direction_len", len(direction)),
			zap.Int("cap", maxImageryDirectionInPrompt),
			zap.String("dropped", direction[maxImageryDirectionInPrompt:]))
	}
	params.Logger.Info("Prepended imagery direction",
		zap.String("site_id", siteID),
		zap.String("kind", kind),
		zap.String("source", directionSource),
		zap.Bool("truncated", truncated),
		zap.String("direction_preview", datahelpers.TruncateString(direction, 100)),
		zap.String("composed_preview", datahelpers.TruncateString(composed, 250)))
	promptTemplate = composed
	promptSource = promptSource + directionSource
}

edits.rationale: The property that actually matters is not the ordering but the survival: 'after truncation at the cap, the palette is still present'. Asserting the survival rather than the string order means a future reordering or cap change cannot silently reintroduce the defect. The package has tests for directionForKind and the override map but none for composition or truncation, which is why this shipped.

grounded_in: generate_image_actions.go:1035 — 'Until provider routing lands, 200 chars is the safe default for the only generation backend (Stability hosted SDXL).' Provider routing HAS since landed (internal/adapters/imagegenerator/routing.go, bugs_open/011) and every declared kind now routes to Banana, whose same comment block estimates '~1000+ char effective'. The code's own stated precondition for revisiting the cap was met and nobody revisited it.
imagery_style_guide.go:136-148 — composeDirection appends medium, then mood, then 'colour palette: '+palette, so the palette is always the tail of the string that is about to be truncated.
generate_image_actions.go:1138 — 'if len(direction) > maxImageryDirectionInPrompt { cut := direction[:maxImageryDirectionInPrompt]' — the truncation is unconditional and unreported.

plan.risks: Behavioural change is limited to sites whose composed direction exceeds 200 chars; below the cap the prompt is identical apart from clause order. Above it, prompts change materially — which is the point — so expect visible change on the next image roll for any site over the cap, robot-hands.com included (233 chars). Its output currently passes an owner gate, so a reviewer should weigh whether reordering it is acceptable: my view is yes, because it gains 'light grey secondary accents only' and loses only prose tail, but I have NOT regenerated robot-hands to prove it and deliberately left its config untouched. Clause order may itself affect model behaviour (leading with colour rather than medium); unmeasured, and worth n>=5 observation rather than assumption. DELIBERATELY NOT PROPOSED: raising the cap. The comment says Banana tolerates ~1000+ chars, so raising it is tempting and would fix this more completely — but choosing a per-provider cap requires provider knowledge in the ACTION layer, and routing.go's own header documents that a second hand-maintained provider list is this codebase's repeat drift class (it shipped content_hero and then hero as separate defects). The bugfix-028 thread rejected the same temptation for the same reason and placed its fold inside the provider. If the council wants the cap raised, it should be a separate change that consults routing rather than duplicating it. INTERACTION with bugs_open/028: its fix folds the avoid list into the positive prompt INSIDE the Banana provider, downstream of this cap, so the two do not contend for the same 200 chars; that thread cites this cap as its reason for going downstream. No conflict expected, but both land in the same image roll and both change every Banana prompt, so attribute any observed change carefully.
